story.title: Backpack Wins Fat Bear Week 2026, Defeating Former Champion Bear 910
story.summary: In the final round of Fat Bear Week 2026, Bear 89, known as Backpack, emerged victorious over Bear 910. The contest, held at Katmai National Park and Preserve in Alaska, saw Backpack win by a margin of just over 5,000 votes, celebrating the resilience of the park's brown bear population.

explore_lenses.label: Who actually won, and was 910 a former champion?
explore_lenses.title: Backpack won; 910 was not a past champion
explore_lenses.summary: Bear 89, Backpack, won the 2026 final by 5,081 votes. The packet’s description of Bear 910 as a former champion is inaccurate: she is the daughter of former champion 409 Beadnose.

claims.text: Backpack received 103,334 votes to 98,253 for Bear 910 in the final, a margin of 5,081 votes.
Explore.org’s bear profiles identify 910 as the daughter of 409 Beadnose, a former Fat Bear Week champion; they do not identify 910 herself as a prior champion.
Backpack is the son of 435 Holly, the 2019 champion, and his nickname originated from his habit as a cub of riding on Holly’s back while crossing the river.

explore_lenses.label: What does Backpack’s win indicate about Katmai?
explore_lenses.title: The contest highlights successful pre-winter feeding
explore_lenses.summary: Fat Bear Week is not a measurement contest or a scientific ranking of individual health; it is a public vote based on visible seasonal change. Organizers frame large fat reserves as important evidence that bears have had access to the salmon needed to endure winter and, for females, potentially support cubs.

claims.text: The National Park Service says Fat Bear Week celebrates bears’ seasonal transformation as they eat salmon and build fat reserves needed to survive winter; the public selects the champion through a bracket tournament.

Explore.org describes Backpack as a medium-large adult male whose relatively nonaggressive approach still gives him access to preferred fishing locations, presenting his body size as evidence that strategy has worked.

Explore.org says 910’s body fat is important to a female bear’s ability to nurse newborn cubs after giving birth in midwinter, while noting only that she appears well-positioned if she gives birth again.

explore_lenses.label: How did 2026 voting differ, and what happens next?
explore_lenses.title: An expanded bracket drew heavy participation
explore_lenses.summary: The 2026 event expanded to 16 bears and encountered enough demand early on that organizers extended voting after access problems. The title is decided, while the bears’ next biological task is preparing for winter rather than participating in any further competition.

claims.text: The National Park Service scheduled the 2026 tournament for September 22-29, with the champion to be crowned September 29, and identified NPS, Explore.org and the Katmai Conservancy as partners.
CBS reported that the bracket expanded from 12 competitors in 2025 to 16 in 2026, and that first-round voting was extended after demand prevented some people from accessing the polls.
The contest’s official bear profiles characterize autumn fat accumulation as preparation for hibernation; Backpack’s win does not confer management action, a prize, or a further competitive round.

story_report.summary: Backpack, bear 89, won Katmai National Park and Preserve’s 2026 Fat Bear Week by defeating bear 910 in the public-voted final. Backpack received 103,334 votes, compared with 98,253 for 910, a 5,081-vote margin. The result crowned Backpack after a tournament celebrating the bears’ autumn effort to build the fat reserves needed to survive winter.

sections.heading: Backpack and Bear 910 Profiles
sections.body: Backpack is the son of 435 Holly, the 2019 Fat Bear Week champion. His nickname dates to his time as a cub, when he rode on Holly’s back while crossing a river. Explore.org describes him as a medium-large adult male who gains access to preferred fishing locations through a relatively nonaggressive approach. Bear 910 is the daughter of 409 Beadnose, another former champion; the profiles do not identify 910 herself as a previous winner.

sections.heading: Fat Bear Week Tournament Context
sections.body: The National Park Service scheduled the 2026 competition for Sept. 22-29, with NPS, Explore.org and the Katmai Conservancy listed as partners. The public selected a champion through a bracket tournament focused on bears’ seasonal salmon feeding and fat accumulation before hibernation. CBS reported that the field expanded from 12 competitors in 2025 to 16 in 2026, and first-round voting was extended after demand prevented some people from reaching the polls.

unresolved.text: The vote result reflects public preference in the contest materials, not either bear’s exact weight, health status or likelihood of surviving winter. Explore.org says 910 appears well-positioned if she gives birth again, but does not establish whether she will.

The supplied sources do not provide a final official audit total for 2026 participation. One account cites more than 2.3 million votes, while the NPS pre-event release cites more than 1.7 million votes cast in 2025.

related_stories.title: UAE President Meets Israeli PM Netanyahu Amid Controversy Over 2023 Attack Warnings
related_stories.summary: The UAE has confirmed that its president met with Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu in Abu Dhabi on Sunday. This meeting follows reports suggesting that the Emirati president had warned Netanyahu about an impending Hamas-led attack on Israel in October 2023, a claim Netanyahu has denied, stating he did not receive any advance warnings from security officials.

related_stories.title: Macron Welcomes Idea of UK's Return to the EU
related_stories.summary: During a joint press conference in Madrid with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, French President Emmanuel Macron expressed that it would be 'excellent news' if the UK decided to rejoin the European Union. He responded positively to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's suggestion about the UK's potential return, saying 'Welcome back' in English.

related_stories.title: Morocco Appoints First Female Prime Minister Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri
related_stories.summary: Morocco's King has appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the country's first-ever female prime minister. El Mansouri, previously the mayor of Marrakesh and a former minister in the coalition government, has been tasked with forming a new government.
